definition: Rejuvenate means to make someone or something fresh and young again.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rejuvenate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rejuvenate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One afternoon thunderstorm rejuvenated the wilted garden, and by dusk every stem stood upright again.
Refresh is a much lighter lift than rejuvenate — a splash of cold water, a ten-minute break, energy topped up for an hour — while rejuvenate hands back youth itself.
Invigorate goes further than refresh — real vigor poured in, a whole afternoon's worth — but it stops short of rejuvenate, which claims the years themselves roll back.

Revive means to bring someone or something back from the edge of stopping — the fainting runner, the stalled campaign — a moment's rescue rather than a transformation. Rejuvenate starts from merely tired or old, never from nearly gone, and it claims far more: youth and freshness handed back.

Renew means to make something like new again, and it attaches most naturally to things, supplies, and promises — a lease, a stock of firewood, a vow. Rejuvenate works on whatever is alive, or spoken of as if it were, and it specifically hands back youth.
